newsitem.title: UK: Chrysalis leaps after upbeat AGM statement.
newsitem.headline: Chrysalis leaps after upbeat AGM statement.

text.p: Shares in Chrysalis Group Plc surged on Wednesday after upbeat comments from the radio, television and music publishing group to shareholders at its annual general meeting.
"During the past year our established music publishing and export businesses have shown extensive growth," said executive chairman Chris Wright.
"The television production companies have moved substantially into profit and all three radio stations have exceeded expectations with each gaining significant audience shares."
Wright said the group would show an expected overall loss in 1997 but radio had reached the end of its investment programme and television would move further into profit.
The stock was quoted 52-1/2p higher at 640 by 1519 GMT.

Chrysalis said its radio stations were well established with revenues at Heart FM in London up 45 percent on last year and Heart Midlands and Galaxy, covering South Wales and the west of England, seeing revenue up over 37 percent in the first quarter.

For the record label Echo, pop group Babybird had scored album and singles successes while the television division had moved into profit, growing to be the second largest independent producer in the UK, Chrysalis said. -- David Holmes, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
